advantages: Ensures every element in an array matches at least one allowed runtime type, returning `true` only when the whole array passes.
Rejects invalid inputs early: returns `false` when `array` or `types` is empty or not a filled array.
Useful for validating mixed-type collections (e.g., numbers and strings) with a single call to `areOneOfType`.

parameterDescriptions.array: An array of elements to verify against the provided types.
parameterDescriptions.types: An array of strings representing the data types to check against.

shortDescription: `areOneOfType` checks whether all elements in a non-empty array are of one of the specified runtime types.
typeScriptHint: This function returns a boolean and does not narrow the array element types at compile time; use it as a runtime validation step before further processing.
useCase: Validate incoming data (e.g., parsed JSON) where a field must be a non-empty array whose items are restricted to a known set of primitive types; return `false` when the array is empty or contains any disallowed type.
